title: Uyen Mai
text: I’m an MD/PhD student in the Medical Scientist Training Program at Case Western Reserve University, now in the PhD phase of my training. My work sits where clinical medicine meets population health. I study how structural conditions such as poverty, neighborhood environment, and access to care shape health, and how community-based programs can address them.

text: I’m an MD/PhD student in the Medical Scientist Training Program at Case Western Reserve University, now in the PhD phase of my training. My work sits where clinical medicine meets population health. I study how structural conditions such as poverty, neighborhood environment, and access to care shape health, and how community-based programs can address them.

title: Uyen Mai
text:
What I’m Working on Now

Community care coordination. Evaluating a community health worker–based Pathways HUB in Northeast Ohio that connects clients to services for health-related social needs, and asking whether that coordination improves health care use and health outcomes.
Implementation science. Studying how the Ask-Advise-Connect tobacco cessation intervention is adapted for food pantries, using the RE-AIM and FRAME-IS frameworks.
Spatial epidemiology. Comparing health outcomes between persistent-poverty and other census tracts and counties across the United States, using CDC PLACES data.

title: Research & Experience
text:
Evaluating community–health system care coordination. The Better Health Pathways HUB coordinates community health workers across Northeast Ohio to help clients meet health-related social needs such as housing, food, and transportation. My work combines interviews with community health workers, care coordination agencies, and health system partners with linked HUB and health care utilization data. The goal is to understand what makes this model work and last, and whether completing social-needs pathways is associated with better health outcomes.
CONNECT-Pantries. An implementation science project with the Prevention Research Center for Healthy Neighborhoods. We analyze focus group data to describe how the Ask-Advise-Connect tobacco cessation intervention is adapted for food pantries, guided by the RE-AIM and FRAME-IS frameworks.
Persistent poverty and health. A national analysis in R comparing CDC PLACES health outcomes between persistent-poverty and other census tracts and counties.
